findings.title: New abstract order() breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: File common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoProvider.java adds abstract `int order();` without a default. Any out-of-tree CryptoProvider that implements the interface will fail to compile and, if already compiled, will fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError when ServiceLoader instantiates it. The method should be a `default` (e.g. return 0) to preserve backward compatibility.

findings.title: Multiple providers silently resolved, ties are arbitrary
findings.body: File common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java previously threw when more than one CryptoProvider was on the classpath. It now sorts by `order()` reversed and returns the first, logging ignored providers only at debug. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, so a classpath containing two of them (a misconfiguration) is now silently resolved by ServiceLoader discovery order instead of failing fast, leading to non-deterministic crypto behavior.

findings.title: readSequence does not reject trailing garbage or check constructed bit
findings.body: File authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java `readSequence()` consumes `length` bytes of content but never verifies the outer buffer is fully consumed, so extra trailing bytes after the SEQUENCE are silently ignored. It also accepts indefinite-length (0x80 returns -1, yielding empty list) and primitive tag 0x10 instead of requiring constructed 0x30. For signature parsing this non-strict DER acceptance enables malleable/forged signatures to pass where strict verification should reject them.

findings.title: Oversized/negative ECDSA integers are truncated instead of rejected
findings.body: File authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java `integerToBytes()` truncates with `System.arraycopy(bytes, bytes.length - qLength, ...)` when `bytes.length > qLength`, and left-pads otherwise, without validating. Combined with `ASN1Decoder.readInteger()` using signed `new BigInteger(bytes)`, a DER signature containing a huge or negative r/s is silently truncated to `signLength/2` bytes and returned as a valid concatenated signature instead of throwing IOException. Attacker-controlled signatures must be rejected, not coerced.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns non-BC provider
findings.body: File authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java `getBouncyCastleProvider()` returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, typically the SUN JKS provider, not a BouncyCastle provider. Callers that expect a BC/BCFIPS provider (registration, algorithms, `BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER`) will get the wrong provider, causing incorrect behavior or failures. It should return null like WildFlyElytronProvider or throw unsupported, not a misleading unrelated provider.

findings.title: Dead ASN1Encoder calls in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
findings.body: File authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java lines 114-115 call `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and the same for sBigInteger and discard the results before building the real sequence on lines 117-121. The dead encodes indicate leftover/copy-paste code and waste work; they should be removed. No input length validation is done either, so a wrong-sized `signature` fails with ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of IOException.

findings.title: Test uses wrong curve and only checks round-trip self-consistency
findings.body: File authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java generates one default `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC")` key (P-256) and reuses it for ES256, ES384 and ES512, then only asserts `asn1->raw->der->raw` round-trips to itself. It never verifies the signature cryptographically, never uses P-384/P-521 keys, known vectors, leading-zero/high-bit r/s cases, or rejection of malformed/trailing/oversized DER, so truncation and strictness bugs are not caught.
